parsed.explanation: No criminalisation of trans identity or same-sex conduct, and gender-identity discrimination has been a criminal offence since 2005 under a broad equality statute covering goods and services and health. Public visibility and support infrastructure are substantial, police record SOGI-motivated suspicions and courts have prosecuted abuse as assault. No documented border, facility, detention or targeting exposure for visitors was provided; entry and facilities remain unresolved rather than protective. Rising reported hate-motivated defamation and assault, plus no hate-crime offence in the penal code, prevent a near-perfect score, but the combined regime is protective rather than hostile.

entry_documents.protection: Discrimination on gender identity is a criminal offence since 2005 and equality law covers goods and services; no visitor-specific border protection documented.
entry_documents.interaction: No documented interaction between foreign documents and entry screening.

federal_state_facilities.protection: Equality statute covers goods and services and health services since 2014 amendment, but facility access is not documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: No documented subnational variation; record warns against manufacturing it.

care_services.exposure: Resident survey, undated, found over 40% of trans respondents unable to access needed care, mainly waiting times; not usable as current visitor prevalence.
care_services.protection: Equality law covers health services; visitor care access not documented.
care_services.interaction: Resident centralised gender units do not establish visitor access.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: No trans criminalisation; penal code has no hate-crime offence, motive only recorded by police.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Same-sex activity legal since 1971; discrimination on gender identity criminalised 2005; gender recognition reformed 2023 as resident climate signal.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Police recording enables monitoring but charge-level remedy for bias motive is not documented.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented for travelling minors or guardians.
minors_guardians.interaction: Resident minor gender-care recommendations do not establish a visitor-facing restriction.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Record-high 1,808 suspected hate crimes, SOGI category rising to 241 over six years and 12% of cases; defamation and assault most common; 2018 LGBT assaults 73. Trans-specific rate not documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Police record and count reported suspicions; first conversion-practices prosecution resulted in convictions as assault.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Raw counts without denominator track reporting volume; they do not show organised visitor targeting.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Entry, passport-marker handling, screening and facility access are explicitly unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Criminal discrimination law and functioning police recording provide some recourse.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Absence of documentation is not treated as safety; known good signals outweigh open questions.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: explicit equality protection, functioning complaints and broad tolerance, with occasional friction and incomplete incident data. This case lacks documented visitor-specific operational details, so not higher.

Higher than this anchor: secondary screening harms are documented there, whereas here no border detention or document-mismatch exposure is documented, and discrimination including gender identity is criminalised.

Lower than this anchor: that case documents trained officials, prompt independent review and compensation. Here facility, border and visitor-care protections are not documented and reported SOGI-motivated assaults are rising.

Higher than this anchor: care refusal required a remedy there. Here no documented visitor care refusal pattern exists, and the undated resident access survey cannot be used as current visitor exposure.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime combines legal protection and visible acceptance with imperfect hate-crime recourse. The most severe documented harms are reported defamation and assault within a broader hate-crime count, not state detention, exclusion or organised targeting. Unresolved entry and facility questions limit certainty, but under the rubric they do not out-vote documented non-criminalisation, anti-discrimination law and functioning recording. For adults travelling alone or with a minor, no age-specific visitor exposure is documented.
